title: Jack Smith and Jeremy Rieger, “Lotus” artwork
lede: A square artwork in gray and violet: a melted-chrome flower in an arched frame, a tall liquid display word, op-art spirals, and Japanese katakana.
summary: Liquid-chrome flower, melted display lettering, violet op-art rings and spirals on a scratched black ground. Jack Smith and Jeremy Rieger.

source.label: AIGA Eye on Design (5 September 2019): “Acid Graphics” Are the New Psychedelia

evidence.note: Inspected the 1200 px image `Lotus-By-Jack-Smith-and-Jeremy-Rieger.jpg` that [Eye on Design](https://eyeondesign.aiga.org/acid-graphics-are-the-new-psychedelia-with-a-heady-dose-of-cynicism/) published with the article, in a scratch folder. Not stored. The object is a digital image as the magazine published it, not a named physical copy. The caption reads “Lotus by Jack Smith and Jeremy Rieger, as featured on @acidgraphix”.

styles.note: Liquid-metal imagery, melted display letters, op-art rings, and horror vacui on black. The accent is violet, not green.

context: [Eye on Design](https://eyeondesign.aiga.org/acid-graphics-are-the-new-psychedelia-with-a-heady-dose-of-cynicism/) shows the work in its 2019 article on acid graphics, with the caption “Lotus by Jack Smith and Jeremy Rieger, as featured on @acidgraphix”.
observed: The ground is black with scratches and dust, like a worn sleeve.
A flower in an arched frame is rendered as melted, reflective gray chrome with hard black contours.
A tall word runs down the left in melted, wavy pale-gray letters, with violet ivy growing over it. Katakana run down the right and across the lower left.
Violet concentric rings form a long capsule at the top. Black-and-white op-art spirals and violet dots run down the right edge.
Small pseudo-script text sits in violet at the lower right.
interpretation: The work has the liquid-chrome surface, the melted lettering, and the op-art patterns of the style in a dense layout. Its violet accent shows that acid green is common but not required.
borrow: Put a liquid-chrome image in an arched frame and surround it with op-art spirals.
Draw one display word as melted, wavy letters and let a plant motif grow over it.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The work is recent and in copyright. The rights holder is the designer or the client.
